findings.title: Single-color gray ink is silently discarded
findings.why_it_matters: A supported DOCX image containing crisp gray or colored text on white can publish with an empty OCR page even though its text is visible. When every foreground pixel has the same nonzero grayscale value, the background-excluding histogram has one occupied bin, every variance is zero, and argmax selects threshold zero; printed_ink therefore becomes false and the printed recognizer is skipped. Handling the singleton histogram explicitly preserves these pixels while retaining the existing threshold behavior for ordinary multilevel scans.

findings.title: OCR acceptance reports forbidden transcription differences as exact
findings.why_it_matters: The new OCR acceptance mechanism can pass and label a German, English or Russian transcription as exact after the model changes capitalization or punctuation, although RAG-67 grants no such exception. For the committed German ground truth 'Die Seerose blüht auf dem Teich.', the different output 'die seerose blüht auf dem teich?' becomes the same case-folded word array, reaches exact=True and requires no user permission. The printed PDF/DOCX gate uses the same lossy comparison, so a wrong punctuation mark can also pass that gate. Comparing independently transcribed tokens while retaining case and punctuation prevents these differences from silently receiving an undeclared allowance.

findings.title: Complete OCR interleaves printed columns
findings.why_it_matters: A two-column printed page processed in complete mode loses Paddle's reading order, even when there is no handwriting. findings.suggested_fix: Give settings rendering a monotonically increasing request generation: capture it before each GET and discard the response unless it remains current. Invalidate outstanding reads when a PATCH starts, and keep refresh/save serialized while that PATCH and its follow-up read finish. Add a browser scenario that holds a revision-0 refresh response, saves and renders revision 1, then releases the older response and verifies the form still shows revision 1 and its limits. findings.title: Fence overlapping settings reads against completed saves
findings.why_it_matters: The administrator can see the old global limits and old saved revision after successfully saving new values. Click refresh while a preview is ready, then save: the refresh GET can capture revision 0, the PATCH and its follow-up GET can render revision 1, and the delayed first GET then unconditionally replaces the form with revision 0. A subsequent preview submits both mutable values from that stale form, potentially restoring an old limit when the administrator only intended to change the other field.
